body:
Thanks! This is a great effort, and I agree we should be making data copying explicit.

However, I don't think we need to make CoW copy constructors explicit. Or at least it's not a high priority right now. Those types don't actually copy data when they're just copy-constructed, so that makes them less dangerous in many situations.
So for now, I would probably leave them (`CowData`, `Vector`, `Array`, `String`) out of the refactor, and focus on the types where we know that the copy construction is costly.

PS. I would have preferred PRs focusing on just one or two types at once, since that makes it a lot easier to review and estimate the effects of. 130 files changed across 8 types (actually more, since you have unrelated copy constructor changes in there too) is just a lot at once. But the above change should make the PR smaller, so maybe that will be enough for me to confidently review it.

Closing as superseded by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115093, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115309, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115646, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116381 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116552.

The only containers covered here that do not have explicit copy constructors are `FixedVector` and `CowData`.
We may address those in the future, but copying either of those does not necessarily imply copying objects or allocations. Therefore, it's more debatable whether they need explicit copy constructors. The same holds for `Array` and `Vector`.
